outcome: umbilical cord blood erythrocyte osmotic fragility
cohort: 151 healthy pregnant women residing in a rural area, along with women from an urban control group, all grouped by delivery type (vaginal or cesarean).
finding: Residing in a rural area with intensive pesticide application was associated with altered placental parameters and lower newborn weight (in cesarean deliveries), and the pesticide spraying season was linked to higher umbilical cord blood erythrocyte osmotic fragility and DNA damage, and lower superoxide dismutase activity.
mod_finding: Placental weight and index were higher in rural groups with vaginal delivery, while newborn weight was lower in the rural spraying season group with cesarean delivery.
cross-section timing: At delivery, across pesticide spraying and nonspraying seasons.
